title: Navigate canonical evidence
instructions: Working directory: repository root; no elevated permissions.
Before running the checker, identify the canonical pages for routes, schema, configuration, and architecture.
Run the checker and inspect the file and link counts.
Open one concept reference and explain why a passing link check does not prove the prose is correct.
Cleanup: none; the checker is read-only.
summary: Use the documentation map and prove that internal references resolve.
evidence: Structured count of Markdown files and internal links, with zero missing targets.
safety: Reads tracked Markdown only; no network or file writes.

title: Locate the repository safely
instructions: Working directory: repository root; ordinary user permissions.
Predict the absolute path reported by the checker and list five required paths.
Run the checker; compare repositoryRoot with pwd or Get-Location.
Explain which listed files are source, configuration, or documentation.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Establish the working directory and distinguish required paths from generated state.
evidence: Repository root and required-path inventory.
safety: Path and existence inspection only.

title: Verify the local toolchain
instructions: Working directory: repository root; no administrator access required.
Predict the Node.js and Git output before running.
Run the checker and compare the Node major with the minimum.
If blocked, install through the platform procedure, reopen the terminal, and rerun.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Prove that Node.js and Git satisfy the minimum environment.
evidence: Redacted version output and prerequisite decision.
safety: Runs only node --version and git --version with a reduced environment.

title: Inspect Git without changing it
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Run git status, branch --show-current, and remote get-url origin yourself; predict the checker result.
Run the checker.
Explain why a nonzero change count is not automatically a failure but must be understood before staging.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Verify repository identity, branch, origin, and ambient working-tree change count.
evidence: Branch, origin, work-tree identity, and change count.
safety: Read-only Git commands; credentials in HTTPS remotes are redacted.

title: Parse every API module
instructions: Working directory: repository root; Node.js installed.
State what node --check can and cannot prove.
Run the checker and inspect exit code and stderr separately.
If it fails, identify the first project file and syntax error before editing.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Use the package script to prove every documented API JavaScript file parses.
evidence: Exit code and parse output for npm --prefix api run check.
safety: Reads source and invokes the fixed package script; it does not start the API or database.

title: Run strict frontend type checking
instructions: Prerequisite: npm --prefix web ci completed. Working directory: repository root.
Predict one failure class the check catches and one runtime issue it cannot catch.
Run the checker.
If blocked, install dependencies; if failed, read the first error file, line, and code.
Cleanup: TypeScript may update ignored build-information state only.
summary: Prove frontend names, props, imports, and interfaces satisfy the TypeScript project.
evidence: TypeScript exit code and diagnostics.
safety: Runs the fixed typecheck script; no build publication or network request.

title: Audit manifest and lock contracts
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Inspect both package.json files and predict direct dependency counts.
Run the checker and inspect nonExactVersions.
Explain why this does not replace npm audit or package provenance review.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Verify exact direct versions and lockfile version 3 for both packages.
evidence: Manifest areas, direct counts, lock versions, and any open ranges.
safety: JSON inspection only.

title: Reconcile public and Express routes
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Before running, explain why /api/health is not an Express path.
Run the checker and inspect route and uniqueness counts.
Find GET /health and one owner route in api/src/server.js.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Derive the Express route count from source and connect it to Caddy prefix behavior.
evidence: 57 unique Express method/path pairs at the documented source commit.
safety: Source inspection only; no HTTP or network activity.

title: Verify API security boundaries
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
List the global and route-specific controls from memory before running.
Run the checker and trace every boolean result to source.
Explain why static presence is not a complete vulnerability audit.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Reconcile global origin handling, owner middleware, JSON limits, parameterized SQL evidence, browser credentials, output encoding, and response headers.
evidence: Structured presence of the documented API and browser security controls.
safety: Reads source and the non-secret example; explicitly never reads api/.env.

title: Derive the persistent entity inventory
instructions: Working directory: repository root; no database required.
Write the 15 table names from the data-model page.
Run the checker and compare the sorted inventory.
Explain why source inventory does not prove a live database has migrated successfully.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Read migration source and reconcile the declared PostgreSQL table count.
evidence: 15 unique CREATE TABLE declarations and names.
safety: Static migration inspection only; no database connection or migration.

title: Verify security and runtime boundaries in source
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Predict every control the checker will seek.
Run the checker and trace each boolean to its source file.
Explain two runtime behaviors this static check cannot prove.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Inspect the static controls that bind the documented request lifecycle and trust model.
evidence: Structured presence of JSON limit, origin middleware, owner middleware, parameterized SQL evidence, credentials include, escaping boundary, and headers.
safety: Read-only static inspection; absence or presence is evidence, not a full vulnerability audit.

title: Classify source and generated paths
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Classify web/src, site/app-assets, site/downloads, node_modules, and api/.env.
Run the checker.
Explain why emptyOutDir false is required and why it also creates housekeeping work.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Verify ignore rules, Vite publication settings, and Nginx SPA fallback.
evidence: Source/generated boundary booleans from .gitignore, Vite, and Nginx.
safety: Read-only configuration inspection.

title: Trace one domain mutation end to end
instructions: Working directory: repository root on a non-release branch; no production mutation.
Choose booking, cancellation, report submission, or report review.
Record the frontend component and API call, middleware, route handler, SQL tables, constraints, audit action, response, and later visible effects.
Compare your trace with repository-guide.md and identify one invariant enforced by PostgreSQL.
Evidence: save the trace in learner notes or a temporary file outside tracked source. Cleanup: remove temporary notes if they contain identifiers.
summary: Trace a real workflow from UI intent through authorization, transaction, side effect, audit, and response.
evidence: A path/symbol trace with at least one authorization boundary, transaction boundary, database invariant, audit action, and response contract.
safety: Code and documentation inspection only; do not call a production mutation.

title: Inspect external-integration controls
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
List every external service and whether browser or API contacts it.
Run the static boundary checker.
Inspect integrations.js timeouts and size limits manually and record values.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Connect provider and browser integration behavior to the static trust controls.
evidence: Static boundary result plus learner-recorded provider timeout and response-size table.
safety: No provider request is made and no credentials are read.

title: Run both API unit-test scripts
instructions: Working directory: repository root; API dependencies installed.
Predict the final verification line from each script.
Run the checker and inspect exit code, stdout, and stderr.
Map one assertion group to its production caller and record what remains untested.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Execute deterministic streak and flight-outcome tests and interpret their verification lines.
evidence: Both fixed unit scripts exit zero and print their verification lines.
safety: Pure local tests; no database or network.

title: Diagnose documentation-link integrity
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Run the checker and inspect files and links checked.
If a failure exists, distinguish missing file from missing heading anchor before editing.
Do not weaken the checker to make a broken link pass.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Use a deterministic checker output as a symptom and explain the correction boundary.
evidence: Zero missing local file and heading-anchor references.
safety: Reads Markdown only; external URLs are not fetched.

title: Scan tracked content for high-risk secrets
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Explain why the checker reports file paths rather than matched secret text.
Run the checker.
If it fails, stop; remove the material from staging/history with owner guidance and rotate any real credential.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Verify that Git does not track environment credentials, private keys, tokens, or credential-bearing URLs.
evidence: Tracked-file count and zero high-risk secret findings.
safety: Reads Git-tracked text only, never api/.env; redacts and never returns matched secret values.

title: Run complete safe pre-deployment validation
instructions: Prerequisite: API and web dependencies installed. Working directory: repository root.
Confirm that the checker does not deploy, migrate, restart, or contact production.
Run the checker; inspect each nested result and any blocked prerequisite.
A pass is pre-deployment evidence only; release and database backups and live verification remain separate.
Cleanup: the isolated build removes its temporary directory automatically.
summary: Execute every non-mutating inspect, validation, typecheck, build, academy, link, and secret check.
evidence: Structured results for every fixed safe checker.
safety: No shell, database, network endpoint, Git mutation, process restart, or publication; isolated output is temporary.

title: Build a read-only operational evidence sheet
instructions: Use a learner-owned environment, or obtain owner authorization before inspecting production.
Record each command from operations.md, its required host and permission, and expected healthy result.
For a provided or observed symptom, map failure to the owning component and name the next read-only diagnostic.
State which actions would affect shared services and require confirmation.
Cleanup: remove any notes containing private host details before sharing.
summary: Prepare and interpret a complete health, process, container, Git, artifact, log, and job-effect inventory.
evidence: A redacted evidence table with component, command, expected result, observed result, interpretation, and escalation boundary.
safety: Read-only commands only; do not restart PM2, Docker, PostgreSQL, Caddy, or auth.

title: Prove a recovery plan without touching production
instructions: Working directory: repository root; use documentation and a scratch database only.
Inventory every state class and its recovery source.
Write the release-backup and pg_dump verification steps with placeholders, not real credentials.
Describe the destructive restore preconditions and a safe isolated restore rehearsal.
Order complete-host recovery and state unrecoverable gaps. Cleanup: destroy only learner-created scratch resources.
summary: Construct a recovery plan that accounts for Git, secrets, database, generated artifacts, downloads, profiles, and shared infrastructure.
evidence: A redacted backup matrix, verification checklist, destructive-restore decision record, and ordered disaster-recovery procedure.
safety: Never restore into production, read api/.env, or restart shared infrastructure for this lab.

title: Verify branch and staging safety
instructions: Working directory: repository root on a feature, fix, or docs branch.
Run git status and inspect intended and ambient work.
Stage only the controlled exercise files, then run the checker.
Unstage the exercise files after recording evidence unless preparing a real contribution.
Cleanup: preserve unrelated work and do not use reset --hard or clean.
summary: Prove the contribution is isolated from release and the staging area excludes secrets and generated output.
evidence: Current branch and staged-path safety decision.
safety: Read-only Git inspection; the checker never stages, commits, resets, cleans, or pushes.

title: Build the frontend in an isolated directory
instructions: Prerequisite: npm --prefix web ci. Working directory: repository root.
Run the checker and inspect emitted app-assets names.
Explain why the output path is safe and what the chunk warning means.
Cleanup is automatic; confirm temporaryOutputRemoved is true.
summary: Compile production-equivalent frontend output without touching site/.
evidence: Vite exit code and temporary asset list.
safety: Writes only to an operating-system temporary directory and removes it.

title: Validate curriculum coverage
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
Run the checker after any academy data change.
Trace one coverage result from concept to questions and lab.
Do not weaken a threshold to conceal missing educational content.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Prove IDs, references, concept assessment coverage, critical evidence, exams, labs, and question quality.
evidence: Academy validation summary with module, concept, question, lab, exam, and capstone counts.
safety: Reads academy data and repository text only.

title: Reconcile the environment-variable inventory
instructions: Working directory: repository root.
List every process.env name before running.
Run the checker and compare source variables with api/.env.example.
Explain why PROFILE_IMAGE_DIR is default-only and why api/.env is never read.
Cleanup: none.
summary: Prove that source, example configuration, and canonical documentation agree on the nine environment variables.
evidence: Source variable names, example keys, and the documented default-only exception.
safety: Reads API source and api/.env.example only; never reads api/.env or prints values.
